project_tracker_diagnostic: Rhizomatous perennial; many narrow 1-strong-veined, commonly V-folded and arching leaves, sessile to short-petioled; usually nearly entire margins; elongated upper-stem head array and long narrow gradually tapered phyllaries.

project_inclusion.learning_reason: Common and useful Central Texas field-learning taxon.

morphology_keys.life_cycle: Rhizomatous perennial; often persists as a colony or patch with multiple shoots in successive seasons.
morphology_keys.habit: Tall upright, usually rough-hairy stems, with leaves numerous along the stem; branching and height vary.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Mostly alternate along the stem; a few lower nodes may be opposite or subopposite. Arrangement alone is not a clean separator from H. annuus.
morphology_keys.leaves: Long narrow lanceolate blades (commonly ca. 10–30 × 2–5.5 cm), usually folded upward along the midrib (conduplicate) and curving/arching outward or downward; margins usually entire, occasionally finely toothed.
morphology_keys.leaf_venation: One dominant visible midvein, often producing a trough- or V-shaped blade; contrast broad commonly 3-basal-veined H. annuus.
morphology_keys.leaf_attachment: Sessile or short-petioled, typically 0–2 cm; inspect a node and compare with the obvious petiole of annual sunflower.
morphology_keys.heads: Usually 3–15 yellow-rayed heads, often spaced up the upper stem in a long raceme- or spike-like pattern, rather than just a terminal branching spray.
morphology_keys.phyllaries: Long narrow lanceolate bracts (ca. 2–3 mm wide), narrowing gradually into thin, long-attenuate tips; inspect mature head sides and undersides.
morphology_keys.fruit: Small flattened cypselas with paired scales/awns; not a reliable split from H. annuus.
best_field_traits: long, narrow, often folded V-shaped blade with one strong midvein
very short leaf stalk or sessile insertion; often nearly untoothed margins
upright rhizomatous perennial, often forming colonies
long slender gradually tapering phyllaries beneath heads

diagnostic_comparison.look_first: Mid-stem leaf: narrow + almost stalkless + one strong midvein + V-folded blade = Maximilian; inspect more than one node.
diagnostic_comparison.confirm_with: Mature flowering heads spaced along upper stem, each with long narrow gradually attenuate phyllaries.
diagnostic_comparison.caution: Some leaves are subopposite; small teeth may occur. Do not diagnose from head color or colony habit alone.

source_audit.scope: Morphology and pairing only. County native-range status left unchanged.
